chunks: And he said: 'O my sons, do not enter from one door but enter from separate doors, and I will remove for you from Allah nothing; indeed the command is only for Allah. Upon Him I have placed my trust, and upon Him let the trusting place their trust.'

key_terms.إِنِ الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ: Indeed the command is only for Allah

ai.seo_question: What advice did Prophet Joseph give his sons regarding entering Egypt?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this advice is interpreted not merely as a tactical security measure to avoid political suspicion, but as a demonstration of 'Hikmah' (wisdom) and the principle of 'Tawakkul' (trust in God) coexisting with practical effort. The phrase 'I do not avail you against Allah' underscores that while human strategy is necessary, ultimate sovereignty and protection reside solely with the Divine, a core tenet in Shia theological understanding of prophetic leadership.
